stem: In the context of neonatal intensive care units (NICU), what is the primary reason coagulase-negative \textit{Staphylococci} (CoNS) frequently cause late onset sepsis?

options.text: Requirement for prolonged intravenous access and ventilation
High rates of maternal colonization during the third trimester
Lack of effective antibiotic prophylaxis for the mother

explanation: Nosocomial infections in the NICU are often linked to the invasive procedures and long-term equipment required for pre-term care.
rationale: Think about the environmental and procedural factors unique to the hospital care of pre-term infants.

optionExplanations.A: Vertical transmission is the mechanism for early onset sepsis, whereas CoNS is typically acquired after birth.
optionExplanations.B: Nosocomial infections in the NICU are often linked to the invasive procedures and long-term equipment required for pre-term care.
optionExplanations.C: CoNS is part of the normal skin flora; the risk in NICU is related to clinical interventions rather than maternal colonization status.
optionExplanations.D: Maternal prophylaxis targets Group B \textit{Streptococcus} to prevent early onset disease, not late onset NICU-acquired infections.

source.hint: Think about the environmental and procedural factors unique to the hospital care of pre-term infants.
